text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: No halt to Har Homa Jewish settlement.
- Israel's top cop tickets himself for using phone while driving.
- 250 million shekels for 50th anniversary celebrations in Israel next year.
- Government to sell 24 percent stake in Bezeq communications; new Bezeq chief is Ami Erel.
- First quarter internal revnue up 4.7 percent.
- ANZ Banking opens Jerusalem branch.
- Tel Aviv, Jerusalem hoteliers forecast sharp drop in spring occupancy.
GLOBES
- Consulting team tells Strauss: Buy Elite. Michael Strauss will decide finally next week.
- Netanyahu: "The economic slowdown -- no longer from recession."
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu: The building on Har Homa will continue. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat ready for summit with prime minister. U.S. to provide Israel with $25 million to fight terrorism.
- Israel freezes its request that the United States hand over Hamas political leader Moussa Abu Marzook.
- Environment Ministry bows to industrialists on air pollution standards.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu: "The era of Israeli gestures is over". His counterterrorism expert will present to Clinton Israeli intelligence on how Arafat gave "green light" to violence.
- U.S. to put at Israel's disposal weapons reserves for quick supply.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Israel captures nine Hamas terrorists on way to carrying out an attack in Israel.
